page: Amazon Web Services i8g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, storage-optimized instance built on the ARMv9 architecture. It features 192 dedicated physical cores powered by AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processors clocked at 2.8 GHz, running without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is substantial, providing 1,536 GB of DDR5 RAM, establishing an 8 GB per core memory footprint. In addition to high CPU and memory density, the server comes bundled with 45,000 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network throughput of 100 Gbps. It contains no discrete GPUs.

Benchmark data reflects exceptional parallel throughput and memory performance across multi-threaded operations. The server lands in the top tier for multi-core stress testing (295,153.48 in stress-ng) and multi-threaded decompression (1,242.06 GB/sec in bzip3). Memory subsystem performance is similarly high, reaching 871.74 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 403.47 GB/sec for writes. Database execution profiles demonstrate top-tier execution, scoring 46,381.73 in PassMark database operations and processing 347.98 million Redis SET operations per second. Static web serving reaches 160.54 GB/sec.

Single-threaded CPU metrics represent a measurable tradeoff, scoring within the average middle tier on Geekbench (1,664.0) and single-core stress-ng (1,647.9). Without GPU acceleration, text generation during large language model inference yields low throughput, recording 7.44 tokens per second on a 7B model. However, high core counts paired with 45 TB of direct-attached NVMe storage provide high qualitative compute-and-storage efficiency per rack unit without hypervisor overhead.

The hardware composition makes AWS i8g.metal-48xl well suited for I/O-intensive database systems, large-scale distributed data stores, distributed compilation pipelines, real-time analytics, and high-throughput Redis caching layers requiring massive local NVMe disk space and broad multi-core concurrency.

It integrates 1,536 GB of DDR5 memory, 45,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a 100 Gbps network interface, operating without GPU acceleration. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate top-tier parallel execution, achieving 295,153.48 in multi-core stress-ng, 871.74 GB/sec in uncached read bandwidth, and 347.98 million Redis SET operations per second. Although single-core compute and LLM generation speeds remain moderate, the high core density and 45 TB direct-attached NVMe volume provide exceptional capacity for high-throughput transactional databases, large distributed caches, software compilation, and real-time big data processing.
